All — I did a quick legal triage on BridgeWork's MSA/DPA. High-level notes (see attached redline):

- Data retention: 90 days for telemetry is okay to discuss but we need explicit language that telemetry excludes raw customer input where customers have opted out of sharing. If they want raw request retention exceptions, that requires SOC2 controls and separate agreement.
- Indemnity & liability: we cannot accept a per-connector cap below our standard platform cap. Propose bridging language: marketplace connectors are "integrations" and governed by the same general cap unless there is intentional misuse.
- DPA: their standard requires a Sub-processor list that is too broad. Request: limit to named sub-processors and a 30-day notice for additions.
- SOW: deliverables/timeline OK but need acceptance criteria and escrow for developer artifacts if contractors are involved.

Attach: BridgeWork_MSA_redline_v1.docx (comments). I flagged sections as "legal-blocker", "commercial-discussion", and "ops-follow-up".

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Team — procurement/finance notes:

- For marketplace connector listings we normally require a contract-first approach for revenue-share clarity. We can do a pilot listing with a PO for SOW work, but recurring referral revenue needs the signed MSA + commercial addendum.
- Revenue-share: 70/30 (their favor) is steeper than our standard. Ben, commercial will push back on anything above 60/40 (partner/redwood) without a clear adoption forecast.
- Tax/withholding: BridgeWork's template has a one-sided withholding clause. Request that this be mutual or clarified per-country.
- Timeline: if legal finalizes redlines by end of week, procurement can prepare a contract skeleton and commercial addendum within 5 business days.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference

Lucia — quick commercial note from marketplace ops:

- We can accept a pilot with 70/30 for the first 3 months if BridgeWork commits to measurable activation KPIs (30 developer sign-ups and 1 active customer integration). After pilot, we move to standard 60/40 unless exceptional volume justifies otherwise.
- We also require a co-marketing credit (50% jointly funded) for marketplace launch promotions.
- For liability carveouts, we can explore a limited per-connector cap for third-party content where BridgeWork exclusively controls connector logic, but need a clear warranty & support SLA in the SOW.

If BridgeWork can agree to a pilot KPI schedule, we can fast-track the listing and revenue reconciliations.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
